stories.title: Rain, snow in northern parts of the country from today
summary: In Punjab and Islamabad, light rain, wind and thunderstorms are expected in the capital city, the Potohar region, Mianwali, Khushab, Bhakkar, Sargodha, Murree and adjoining areas on Wednesday (today).
Rain, wind and thunderstorms are also expected in Dera Ghazi Khan, Layyah, Bhakkar and Multan on Nov 12.

However, isolated rain, wind and thunderstorms, accompanied by hailstorms, are expected in Duki, Harnai, Pishin, Sherani, Surab, Zhob, Barkhan, Musakhel, Quetta, Ziarat, Chaman, Qila Abdullah, Qila Saifullah, Kalat and Khuzdar on the night of Nov 11 and Nov 12.

stories.title: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Hegseth
summary: Republicans in the US House of Representatives blocked an effort on Tuesday to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, winning a reprieve for the polarising Pentagon chief before Democrats take control of Congress next year and possibly try again.

The vote on a procedural motion came just hours after Hegseth blasted efforts to impeach him as a farce and delivered a defiant defence of his record at the helm of the US military, winning praise from US President Donald Trump.
Hegseth calls himself secretary of war, part of his effort to rebrand a military he said was too weak and “woke” when he took office last year.

stories.title: Public Accounts Committee seeks to delay power firms’ sell-off until asset valuation
summary: The proposal came after Auditor General of Paki­stan Maqbool Ahmad Gon­dal raised concerns that the government was relying on outdated valuations of public assets during a meeting of the PAC to examine the audit reports of the Power Division and its attached entities for 2024-25.
She called for another meeting in three weeks to review the privatisation process and ensure that the assets were assigned their correct market values before further steps were taken.
The Privatisation Commission and the Power Division were directed to submit detailed reports at the next meeting.

stories.title: Development spending stalls despite surplus
summary: Total PSDP spending in the first four months (July-October) of 2026-27 amounted to Rs103.87bn — 10.4pc of the Rs1trillion allocation, according to the Ministry of Planning and Development.

Latest data released by the Ministry of Planning and Development showed that, excluding corporations, total PSDP expenditure by about 33 ministries and divisions amounted to a meagre Rs74.65bn in the first four months, or about 11pc of the total allocation of Rs682bn.

Combined spending in provinces and special areas (Azad Kashmir and GB) for development amounted to Rs23.8bn, or just 10pc of the annual allocation of Rs233bn and the Planning Commission’s authorisation of Rs59.8bn for the first four months.

stories.title: Pakistan pushing for diplomacy amid global tensions
summary: With regard to the Middle East, the foreign minister said Pakistan’s facilitation of the Islamabad talks between the United States and Iran in April had reflected its commitment to resolving conflicts through dialogue.

Noting that nothing is going to change in the relationship between Pakistan and India, Prof Mearsheimer said that India could not become a great power in the near future, as it is plagued by too many issues, though it could become a formidable middle power, like Japan.

However, he maintained that Israel had an expansionist agenda and the war between Israel and Iran was still unfinished, adding that a military alliance between India, UAE and Israel could pose a threat to Pakistan.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz arrives in Turkiye to address COP31 summit
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif arrived in Antalya, Turkiye, on Tuesday for a three-day visit to attend the Leaders’ Summit of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP 31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

At the COP31 Leaders’ Summit, PM Shehbaz will highlight Pakistan’s climate priorities and emphasise the urgent need for enhanced global climate action and strengthened international cooperation to mitigate the adverse impacts of climate change, PMO said.

Under UN climate agreements, developed countries, which are historically responsible for most greenhouse gas emissions, have provided financial support to help developing nations adapt to climate impacts and transition to cleaner energy.

stories.title: US calls for new Europe security framework as Russia, Ukraine hold first peace talks in 9 months
summary: A first day of US-led talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi ended on Tuesday, with Washington calling for a “new” security framework, as Europe fears US President Donald Trump plans a deal with Moscow on the continent’s future.
At the Abu Dhabi talks, Trump’s son-in-law Kushner said the US hoped to “create a new framework” of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that will secure “decades, if not centuries, of peace”.

Ukraine has warned against a “Yalta 2.0”, referring to Western leaders dividing Europe with the Soviet Union after World War II, and the EU has said security arrangements can only be discussed after a ceasefire. “Putin wants the USSR back,” Zelensky told Danish media.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz stresses clean energy’s importance for Pakistan at Chashma-5 nuclear plant event
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has emphasised that Chashma-5 (C-5) Nuclear Power Plant represents clean electricity and energy security for the people of Pakistan.
According to PID, PAEC Chairman Dr Raja Ali Raza Anwar highlighted that nuclear power plays an important role in Pakistan’s energy security by providing reliable and low-carbon electricity.
He added that Pakistan’s nuclear power plants safely and efficiently generate 3,530MW of electricity, avoiding 15 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually, the press release read.

stories.title: Second Pakistan-Sri Lanka Test shifted from Lahore to Rawalpindi over smog
summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Tuesday shifted the second Test between Pakistan and Sri Lanka from Lahore to Rawalpindi amid worsening smog conditions in the Punjab capital.
The venue change means both Tests of the two-match series will now be played at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.
Sri Lanka have been touring Pakistan since early October.

stories.title: Faysal Quraishi responds to 'Mango Jutt' criticism
summary: Film festivals are not just about watching movies; they also provide filmmakers, artists and enthusiasts an opportunity to connect, exchange ideas and learn about the process of filmmaking.

Asked about the audience response after his film was screened at the cinema and later at the World Culture Festival, as well as the criticism it received on social media following its release, the filmmaker said that many viewers had enjoyed the film.
"Some people praised the film, while others did not like it.

stories.title: Pakistan beat Nepal to set up U-19 Asia Cup semi-final against Bangladesh
summary: Batting first, Pakistan posted 275-7 in their allotted 50 overs, with half-centuries from Ahmed Hussain and captain Farhan Yousaf laying the foundation for the total.
For Nepal, Bipin Sharma took three wickets for 58 runs.
Ahmed completed an impressive all-round performance, claiming four wickets for 35 runs in his 10 overs.

stories.title: Israel's parliament sworn in as Eisenkot tries to forge a government
summary: Israel’s parliament was sworn in on Tuesday without a new government, after a deadlocked general election stripped Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his parliamentary majority but left his main rivals with no clear path to power.
But they have potential allies in Israel’s Arab-led parties, which hold 19 seats and are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu.

Eisenkot could secure the threshold with support from Arab-Israeli lawmakers, who secured a record number of seats on the back of anger in the minority community over Netanyahu’s hard-right government.

stories.title: Rs5tr spent in defiance of law
summary: The federal government has "unconstitutionally" spent over Rs5 trillion on ministries functioning in the provincial domain since the 18th Amendment, according to proceedings of a Senate functional committee panel that on Tuesday barred the release of any further funds for them.
The committee instructed the Ministry of Finance, the auditor general and the accountant general to stop releasing funds to ministries working in violation of the Constitution.
For one minister and one federal secretary a ministry is retained in devolved areas, which resulted in over Rs5 trillion of spending in 16 years in violation of the Constitution, he said.

stories.title: PSX jumps 5,449 points in spectacular rally
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) staged a powerful rally on Tuesday as investors returned from the long weekend with renewed buying interest, driving the KSE-100 index up by over 5,400 points amid support from strong remittances and easing international oil prices.
"Going forward, the market is likely to maintain its bullish momentum amid easing oil prices and improved global risk appetite.

Topline Securities observed that investor sentiment remained upbeat amid easing international oil prices and diminishing concerns over a potential escalation in geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran.

stories.title: Pakistan backs global green freight push
summary: He said international freight transport was the lifeblood of global commerce but one of the fastest-growing sources of transport-related greenhouse gas emissions, and that economic growth and environmental stewardship were mutually reinforcing goals.
The minister reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to decarbonising global supply chains and building climate-resilient logistics infrastructure.

He said TIR transit volumes had risen 200% under the UN TIR Convention, with digital pre-shipment notices integrated into the Pakistan Single Window and an eTIR project with UNECE, positioning Pakistan as one of the fastest-rising countries in regional trade facilitation.

stories.title: Import-centric auto policy under fire
summary: Pakistan's newly announced auto policy has drawn strong criticism from the domestic automotive parts industry, which warns that its import-centric approach could undermine local manufacturing, threaten 300,000 direct jobs and increase pressure on foreign exchange reserves.

He suggested renaming it from the "Auto and Auto Parts Policy" to the "Policy for Automobile Assembly and Import of New and Used Vehicles", arguing its incentives primarily benefited imports rather than local manufacturing.

Aizaz also raised concerns over concessions for new energy vehicles, particularly the proposed 15% localisation target over five years, saying low import duties on electric vehicles and components could shift manufacturing and employment abroad.

stories.title: Remittances nearly cover trade gap
summary: Pakistan's workers' remittances rose to a four-month high of $3.9 billion in October, taking cumulative inflows during the first four months of FY27 to $14.77 billion, almost enough to cover the country's entire merchandise trade deficit of $14.6 billion during the same period.

According to data released by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Tuesday, October remittances increased 13.8% year-on-year from $3.42 billion and rose 8.5% month-on-month from $3.59 billion in September, the highest monthly inflow recorded so far in FY27.
Inflows from the United States increased 13.8% to $1.26 billion, while remittances from European Union countries rose 9.6% to $1.87 billion.

stories.title: Bilawal calls for unity via ‘political reset’, urges PM to build trust with allies and opposition
summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Tuesday called for a “political reset”, wherein all political parties must unite for the sake of the country, while also urging the prime minister to take measures to build trust with the government’s allies and the opposition.

On its part, the Centre has repeatedly cited the KP government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the counterterrorism fight for its decision, following which the PPP’s governor now heads the provincial administration.
As he highlighted the efforts of the Sindh government post the 2022 floods, Bilawal particularly thanked the premier for the Centre’s support in the flood rehabilitation projects.

stories.title: JI says 'basic outline' of proposal for petroleum levy relief agreed upon during talks with govt
summary: ISLAMABAD: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) Vice Emir Liaqat Baloch said on Tuesday that the government and the party had agreed on the “basic outlines” of a proposed agreement as the two sides held their 10th round of negotiations on petroleum levy relief.

After a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif last month, both sides agreed to form a bipartisan committee to expand the government’s ongoing fuel relief scheme in response to JI’s demands for the abolition of the petroleum levy.
As per the statement, Baloch said the government also acknowledged that the demand for abolition of the petroleum levy was justified and could result in substantial relief for the public.

stories.title: Pakistan tighten grip on first Test as Sri Lanka struggle at 114-3
summary: Pakistan strengthened their hold on the opening Test against Sri Lanka on Tuesday, declaring their first innings at 434 for nine before reducing the visitors to 114 for three at the close of the second day at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium.
Sri Lanka, who still trail by 320 runs, will resume their innings on the third day with Kamindu Mendis unbeaten on 40 and Dhananjaya de Silva on 22.
Pakistan will resume on the third day firmly in control, with a substantial first-innings lead and three Sri Lankan wickets already in hand.

stories.title: ‘Hatred should come to an end’: Gohar defends interaction with ex-army chief Bajwa amid criticism
summary: PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Tuesday defended his brief interaction with former army chief Gen Qamar Javed Bajwa, saying political hostilities should end, and clarified that the two had merely exchanged greetings at a wedding.
Meanwhile, Gohar rejected the possibility of PTI boycotting the upcoming local government elections, saying the party would participate like other political parties.
Gohar welcomed the Islamabad High Court's order regarding meetings with incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, expressing hope that it would be implemented this time.

stories.title: Embattled Pentagon chief slams impeachment effort as 'farce'
summary: Trump has backed Hegseth so far, and on Tuesday wrote on social media that the Pentagon chief “gets an ‘A’ plus, plus, plus for his defence” against the impeachment efforts.

Hegseth on Tuesday defended military interventions in Yemen, Iran and Venezuela as well as strikes targeting alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific. ‘Would do it again’ “I stand behind every one of these operations.
Several of the articles of impeachment relate to the Iran war, accusing Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, which requires congressional consultation on US military interventions.

stories.title: Centre spent Rs5tr on devolved subjects in violation of Constitution, Senate panel head says
summary: During a meeting of that sub-committee last month, senators sought a probe into a staggering Rs2.6 trillion expenditure by the federal government on education and health ministries.

The FIA informed the committee that 512 notices had been issued to various companies in connection with the ongoing investigation, out of which 19 companies joined the proceedings with partial records, while more than 100 notices were returned or remained undelivered.

The panel was also briefed about the FBR’s reluctance to share relevant records with the parliamentary committee, particularly when the department was prepared to provide information to the court and other authorities.

stories.title: TV anchor's killing: Court extends physical remand of victim's husband by 4 days
summary: RAWALPINDI: The physical remand of the husband of anchorperson Rabia Ahsan, who was shot dead at home in the Gulshanabad area earlier in the week, was extended by four days by a court on Tuesday.
He urged the court to extend the remand by seven days in order to interrogate the suspect and complete the investigation.
The court subsequently extended the remand by four days to facilitate the investigation and directed the investigating officer to produce the accused on Nov 14.

stories.title: JI, govt agree on draft outlines for petroleum levy relief
summary: The government and JI held a 10th round of talks on the petroleum levy, with both sides agreeing on the need to provide relief to consumers, particularly low-income households, while discussions on a phased reduction of the levy also came under discussion.
On September 12, JI chief announced a long march towards Islamabad for September 20, warning that the party would intensify its campaign if the government did not abolish the levy.

The JI chief then gave the government 10 days to abolish the petroleum levy and provide meaningful relief to the inflation-hit public, warning that his party would resume its long march towards Islamabad in mid-November if its demands were not met.

stories.title: Imran's hospital transfer: Uzma seeks early fixation of contempt plea against govt for third time
summary: The SC’s office has already turned down Uzma’s two previous requests for an early hearing of the contempt plea, which was filed on Aug 22.

The application stated the previous contempt plea had also sought court directives to arrange and facilitate weekly meetings between Imran and his family members, including petitioners and his other sisters, Noreen Niazi and Aleema Khan, along with his cousin Qasim Zaman.

On Sept 16, resuming the hearing on petitions concerning Imran’s health, the SC had expressed reservations over the Federal Constitutional Court’s (FCC) directive that cases pertaining to the PTI founder’s hospital transfer be fixed before it.

stories.title: Britain says its bases are safe after US refuelling planes evacuated
summary: Britain said on Tuesday that its military bases were safe, after the US removed huge refuelling aircraft from a British airbase following what the Wall Street Journal said was a threat from Iran, the second such apparent evacuation in three months.
In September, the US removed bombers that had been used to strike Iran from another British base, RAF Fairford, on security grounds after a group of men approached the base in white vans.

The US upgraded the security posture at RAF Mildenhall and another UK base, RAF Lakenheath, to FPCON Charlie, the second-highest defensive threat level, the Wall Street Journal report said, citing a US official familiar with the matter.

stories.title: NAB issues second notice to JUI-F chief's son over alleged 'illegal appointments' in Pakistan Post
summary: NAB officials declared his response unsatisfactory and issued a fresh notice, directing him to appear in person at 11am on Friday.
NAB had earlier summoned Rehman's son on November 5 over alleged irregularities in the appointments at the PPOD during his tenure.
According to the earlier NAB notice, the Establishment Division had authorised recruitment against 3,938 posts at the Pakistan Post Office, but 4,252 people were allegedly appointed.

stories.title: Petrol drops by Rs8, diesel by Rs7 for Nov 11
summary: The federal government on Tuesday slashed the price of petrol by Rs8 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7 per litre for November 11.
Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.

stories.title: Lawyer says Shah Mahmood Qureshi taken to hospital days after suffering fall
summary: LAHORE: The lawyer representing Shah Mahmood Qureshi said on Tuesday that the senior PTI leader, who is currently incarcerated at Kot Lakhpat jail, was taken to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) days after suffering a fall.
Speaking to Dawn, his counsel Rana Mudassar Umar said: “[Qureshi] was taken to PIC today as he fainted and suffered a fall a few days ago.
On Nov 6, a meeting of the PTI core committee also expressed concern over Qureshi’s “fall and the resulting impact on his health”.

stories.title: Uzma moves SC for early hearing of Imran's medical transfer case
summary: Read: PTI seeks Imran's immediate transfer to Shifa International Hospital over renewed blood pressure concern Uzma had already filed a contempt petition against the prime minister and other executive authorities over their alleged failure to implement the August 18 order.
On September 14, the FCC had summoned the record of the case concerning Imran's health from the SC.
Also Read: Gohar demands immediate implementation of SC order on Imran's medical treatment Despite two months having passed, the SC has not fixed the matter for hearing.

stories.title: Wapda says no threat to Tarbela Dam's integrity, critical structures after rock collapse at project site
summary: The consultants, contractor and Wapda project management briefed him on the current situation and the measures taken so far,” it said.
According to the handout, the Wapda chairman directed the consultants to submit a detailed report covering all aspects of the incident at the earliest.

He further directed the consultants, contractor and Wapda project team to execute remedial measures immediately, and to finalise the contingency plan to minimise the delay in the overall completion of the project due to the incident.

stories.title: 13 Pakistanis dead in Greek detention since 2000: report
summary: The report said that at least 112 foreign nationals in total had died in police and immigration detention facilities in Greece since 2000, with authorities failing to maintain a reliable public record of the deaths.

Researchers said Greek authorities do not routinely publish statistics on the number of foreign nationals who die in custody, their identities, the locations of their deaths or the circumstances surrounding them.

Researchers highlighted significant gaps in information about people who died in state custody, saying basic details about their identities and the circumstances of their deaths remained undocumented even though they had been held by state authorities.

stories.title: Shah Mahmood rushed to Punjab Institute of Cardiology after reported prison collapse
summary: Senior PTI leader Shah Mahmood Qureshi was on Tuesday transferred to Lahore's Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) after reportedly collapsing inside Kot Lakhpat jail, prompting his family to seek urgent medical investigations and treatment.
I learnt of my father Shah Mahmood Qureshi's fall from family after they met him in Kot Lakhpat jail today.
Previously held at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi, Qureshi was moved to Kot Lakhpat Jail last year due to logistical concerns over frequent court appearances in Lahore.

stories.title: Lahore’s PM2.5 level eight times WHO guideline, report says
summary: Lahore’s average PM2.5 concentration stood at 126 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, exceeding the 24-hour National Environmental Quality Standards (NEQS) on all 40 days for which valid data were available.

Lahore’s average PM2.5 concentration between 6pm on Nov 8 and 1am on Nov 10 was 234 micrograms per cubic metre, 10pc higher than the average recorded during the same hours over the preceding seven days.
The average increase in the four border cities — Lahore, Kasur, Sialkot and Narowal — was 36 micrograms per cubic metre, compared with 85 micrograms in Faisalabad and Multan.

stories.title: Political narratives and allegations have a limited 'shelf life', CM Maryam says
summary: JHELUM: Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Tuesday said political narratives, allegations and criticism had a limited “shelf life”, asserting that public service and development work ultimately determined electoral success.

She said she was answerable to the people for the expenditure of public money, adding that she would not spare any minister or official against whom evidence of corruption or bribery was presented. “I have not said that corruption has completely ended in Punjab,” she said.
On Friday, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif claimed that Salik’s recent corruption allegations against the Punjab government are part of efforts to set the ground for an “alternative arrangement”.

stories.title: BHC hands ex-MPA Abdul Majeed Achakzai 10-year sentence in traffic cop hit-and-run case
summary: QUETTA: The Balochistan High Court on Tuesday handed former MPA Abdul Majeed Achakzai a ten-year sentence in a case regarding the death of a traffic policeman in a hit-and-run incident.

A division bench comprising Justice Muhammad Amir Nawaz Rana and Justice Abdul Qayyum Lehr allowed an appeal filed by the provincial government against Achakzai’s acquittal and set aside the local court decision dated September 4, 2020.
However, in 2020, a local court in Quetta acquitted him in the case.
